gap: Give the world continuous grounded landscape depth: smooth terrain materials and contour silhouettes with believable near/mid/far separation. Faceted card foliage and broad polygon verge/shoulder planes remain the dominant mismatch in every view.
secondary_gaps: Golden hour remains pale and low-contrast, missing the bar's saturated warm fields and coherent long shadows.
Night has stars and a visible road, but the headlight pool and blue ambient terrain separation are much weaker than the bar.
Winter communicates a white palette yet leaves exposed shoulder polygons and patchy ground instead of continuous snow relief.
Cockpit framing is recognizable but the oversized dark dashboard and simplified interior lack the bar's mirror/A-pillar realism.
The elevated vista has a readable road and bridge, but no water-backed composition or layered atmospheric ridges comparable to the bar.

evidence.note: Bar's broad lake-backed hills, continuous grass and authored car read as a finished landscape. Ours has a legible road and dense clumps but faceted crowns, repeated cards and conspicuous flat pale verge.
Bar wins with saturated amber fields, controlled low sun and long shadows. Ours is washed toward the sun, with gray-green ground and weak shadow structure despite a readable chase car.

Ours supplies stars, tail lights and a visible ribbon, but most terrain collapses into dark low-poly silhouettes. Bar retains shoreline/mountain context, a blue night ramp and a strong headlight cone.
Bar has a credible mirror, A-pillar, road and hillside under flat cloud light. Ours establishes a cockpit, but the dark slab dashboard fills the lower frame and autumn vegetation is visibly faceted.
Bar is a coherent snow world with snow-shaped relief. Ours changes trees and ground toward white but leaves exposed polygon shoulder patches and a normal dark road.

Bar's elevated coastal frame has smooth cut slope, water and multiple atmospheric ridge layers. Ours has a readable elevated road/bridge but remains a flat green patchwork with no water or comparable depth.

Bar's driver view is restrained and photographic with mirror, A-pillar and road cut. Ours has a centered road and detailed wheel, but noisy dark interior, oversized dash and low-poly verge are unmistakable.

verdict_text: Independent round-14 seven-shot blind review: the official bar wins all seven comparisons and the randomized side call is correct 7/7. Ground-material blending and contact shading are present, but the global read remains procedural low-poly scenery: faceted foliage and hard polygon verge planes erase the continuous landform depth of the reference.
